Chapter 6

Triangles

Exam weight: 6 marks (1 Assertion-Reason + 1 SA-I + 1 SA-II) | Dropped: Areas of Similar Triangles, Pythagoras Theorem

Concept Notes

  • Similar triangles: same shape — corresponding angles equal, corresponding sides proportional.
  • Criteria for similarity: AA (two angles equal), SSS (all sides proportional), SAS (one angle equal + sides on either side proportional).
  • Basic Proportionality Theorem (Thales): a line parallel to one side of a triangle, intersecting the other two sides, divides them in the same ratio.
  • Converse of BPT: if a line divides two sides of a triangle in the same ratio, it is parallel to the third side.

Assertion–Reason (1 mark) — 5 Qs

  1. A: If DE∥BC in ΔABC with D on AB, E on AC, then AD/DB = AE/EC. R: This follows from the Basic Proportionality Theorem. (Fig. T1)
  2. A: In ΔPQR, if PS/SQ = PT/TR then ST∥QR. R: This is the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem. (Fig. T2)
  3. A: Two triangles are similar if their corresponding angles are equal. R: This is the AA criterion for similarity of triangles. (Fig. T4)
  4. A: In ΔABC, D and E are midpoints of AB and AC; therefore DE∥BC and DE = ½BC. R: The Midpoint Theorem is a special case of the Basic Proportionality Theorem. (Fig. T1)
  5. A: If in ΔABC and ΔDEF, AB/DE = BC/EF = CA/FD, then ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. R: This is the SAS criterion for similarity of triangles. (Fig. T4)

SA-I (2 marks) — 7 Qs

  1. In trapezium PQRS, PQ∥SR, diagonals intersect at O. If OP=6cm, OQ=8cm, OR=9cm, find OS. (Fig. T3)
  2. In ΔABC, DE∥BC, AD=4cm, DB=6cm, EC=9cm. Find AE. (Fig. T1)
  3. In ΔPQR, S and T are on PQ, PR such that ST∥QR. If PS=4cm, SQ=5cm, TR=10cm, find PT. (Fig. T2)
  4. In ΔABC, D is a point on AB such that AD = ¼AB. A line through D parallel to BC meets AC at E. Find AE:EC. (Fig. T1)
  5. In ΔLMN, D and E are points on LM, LN respectively such that DE∥MN. If LD=3, DM=x−2, LE=6, EN=x+1, find x. (Fig. T1)
  6. ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. If AB=6cm, DE=9cm, BC=8cm, find EF. (Fig. T4)
  7. In ΔABC, DE∥BC. If AD=x+3, DB=x, AE=x+5, EC=x+1, find x. (Fig. T1)

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs — Prove

  1. State and prove the Basic Proportionality Theorem. (Fig. T1)
  2. Prove the converse of the Basic Proportionality Theorem. (Fig. T1)
  3. In trapezium ABCD, AB∥CD, diagonals intersect at O. Prove that AO/OC = BO/OD. (Fig. T3)
  4. D is a point on side BC of ΔABC such that ∠ADC = ∠BAC. Prove that CA² = CB × CD. (Fig. T5)
  5. In ΔABC, D and E are points on AB, AC such that DE∥BC. Prove that ΔADE ~ ΔABC. (Fig. T1)
  6. In ΔABC and ΔDEF, AB/DE = AC/DF and ∠A = ∠D. Prove that ΔABC ~ ΔDEF. (Fig. T4)
  7. Prove that the ratio of any two corresponding sides of two equiangular triangles is the same as the ratio of their corresponding perimeters. (Fig. T4)
  8. ABCD is a trapezium with AB∥DC. E and F are points on sides AD and BC respectively such that EF∥AB. Show that AE/ED = BF/FC. (Fig. T6)

Chapter 7

Coordinate Geometry

Exam weight: 6 marks (1 VSA + 1 SA-I + 1 SA-II) | Dropped: Area of a Triangle — no such questions anywhere below

Concept Notes

  • Distance formula: d = √[(x₂−x₁)² + (y₂−y₁)²]
  • Section formula (point dividing AB in ratio m:n internally): ((mx₂+nx₁)/(m+n), (my₂+ny₁)/(m+n))
  • Midpoint = section formula with ratio 1:1.
  • Collinearity and special triangles are shown using the distance formula only (equal sides, Pythagoras relation, or equal slopes) — never the area formula (dropped for Level 1).

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. Find the distance between (3,4) and (7,1). (Fig. CG1)
  2. Find the midpoint of the segment joining (2,−3) and (6,7).
  3. Find the distance between P(2,3) and Q(6,3).
  4. Find the point dividing the join of (1,2) and (7,8) in ratio 1:2. (Fig. CG2)
  5. Find the distance of the point (5,12) from the origin.
  6. If the midpoint of (x,4) and (2,y) is (3,5), find x and y.
  7. Find k if the distance between (2,k) and (2,5) is 3.
  8. Find the ratio in which (4,5) divides the segment joining (2,3) and (7,8).
  9. Find the distance between A(−2,−3) and B(3,9).
  10. (1,2), (4,y), (x,6), (3,5) are vertices of a parallelogram taken in order. Find x and y. (Fig. CG3)

SA-I (2 marks) — 6 Qs

  1. Find k if P(2,k) is equidistant from A(3,4) and B(1,0).
  2. If the distance between P(x,3) and Q(4,7) is 5, find x.
  3. Find the ratio in which the y-axis divides the segment joining (−3,4) and (5,6).
  4. Find the coordinates of the point dividing the join of (−1,7) and (4,−3) in ratio 2:3.
  5. Find the point on the x-axis equidistant from (2,−5) and (−2,9).
  6. Find R which divides the segment joining P(−4,0) and Q(0,6) such that PR = ¾ PQ.

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs

  1. Find the ratio in which P(x,2) divides the segment joining A(12,5) and B(4,−3); also find x.
  2. R(x,y) divides the segment joining P(1,3) and Q(2,7) internally in ratio 3:4. Find R.
  3. If A(2,3), B(4,k), C(6,−3) are collinear, find k. (Fig. CG7)
  4. Prove that (3,0), (6,4), (−1,3) are the vertices of a right-angled isosceles triangle. (Fig. CG4)
  5. Find the coordinates of the points of trisection of the segment joining A(2,−2) and B(−7,4).
  6. A(1,2), B(4,y), C(x,6), D(3,5) are vertices of a parallelogram taken in order. Find x and y. (Fig. CG3)
  7. Find the coordinates of a point equidistant from A(5,3), B(5,−5), C(1,−5). (Fig. CG6)
  8. Show that A(1,1), B(−1,−1), C(−√3,√3) are the vertices of an equilateral triangle. (Fig. CG5)

Chapter 10

Circles

Exam weight: 4 marks (2 VSA + 1 SA-I) | No SA-II/LA for this chapter — matches exam exactly

Concept Notes

  • Exactly two tangents can be drawn from an external point to a circle, and they are equal in length.
  • The tangent at any point is perpendicular to the radius through the point of contact.
  • Tangent length from external point at distance d (radius r): L = √(d²−r²)
  • For a quadrilateral circumscribing a circle: AB + CD = BC + DA.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. Two tangents PA, PB from external point P; if ∠APB=70°, find ∠AOB. (Fig. C1)
  2. Tangent length from an external point is 24cm, radius 7cm. Find the distance of the point from the centre. (Fig. C1)
  3. A point is 17cm from the centre of a circle of radius 8cm. Find the tangent length. (Fig. C1)
  4. Two concentric circles have radii 5cm and 3cm. Find the length of a chord of the larger circle that touches the smaller. (Fig. C2)
  5. If the radius is 6cm and the tangent length is 8cm, find the distance from the centre to the external point. (Fig. C1)
  6. From an external point, the angle between two tangents is 60°. Find the angle between the two radii to the points of contact. (Fig. C1)
  7. PA and PB are tangents from P. If PA=5cm, find PB. (Fig. C1)
  8. A circle has radius 5cm; an external point is 13cm from the centre. Find the tangent length. (Fig. C1)
  9. Two tangents from an external point subtend an angle of 90° at the centre. If the tangent length is 10cm, find the radius. (Fig. C1)
  10. A circle touches all four sides of quadrilateral ABCD. If AB=6cm, CD=8cm, find AD+BC. (Fig. C3)

SA-I (2 marks) — 7 Qs

  1. ABCD is a quadrilateral, ∠D=90°. A circle centre O touches AB, BC, CD, DA at P, Q, R, S. If BC=30cm, CD=17cm, BP=20cm, find the radius. (Fig. C3)
  2. Two tangents TP, TQ from external point T, ∠PTQ=100°. Find ∠OPQ. (Fig. C1)
  3. PQ is a chord of length 8cm in a circle of radius 5cm. The tangents at P and Q meet at T. Find TP. (Fig. C1)
  4. A circle is inscribed in ΔABC with AB=12cm, BC=10cm, CA=8cm, touching the sides at P, Q, R. Find the tangent lengths from each vertex. (Fig. C4)
  5. An external point is 13cm from the centre of a circle of radius 5cm. Find the area of the quadrilateral formed by the two tangents and the two radii. (Fig. C1)
  6. Tangent segments PA, PB are drawn from external point P with ∠APB=120° and OP=10cm. Find PA. (Fig. C1)
  7. A circle touches all four sides of quadrilateral ABCD. If AB=6cm, BC=7cm, CD=4cm, find DA. Then prove the general result AB+CD=AD+BC. (Fig. C3)

Chapter 12

Areas Related to Circles

Exam weight: 5 marks (2 VSA + 1 SA-II) | Dropped: Areas of Combinations of Plane Figures

Concept Notes

  • Sector area = (θ/360°) × πr²  |  Arc length = (θ/360°) × 2πr  |  also Sector area = ½ × r × arc length
  • Segment area = Sector area − Area of the triangle (formed by the two radii and the chord)
  • Take π = 22/7 and √3 = 1.73 unless stated otherwise.

VSA (1 mark) — 10 Qs

  1. Find the area of a sector of radius 7cm and angle 60°. (Fig. A1)
  2. Find the circumference of a circle whose area is 154 cm².
  3. Find the length of an arc of a circle of radius 21cm subtending 60° at the centre. (Fig. A1)
  4. Find the area of a semicircle of radius 14cm. (Fig. A2)
  5. Find the perimeter of a sector of radius 10cm and angle 90°. (Fig. A3)
  6. A pendulum swings through 45° and describes an arc of 11cm. Find the length of the pendulum. (Fig. A4)
  7. Find the area of a quadrant of a circle whose circumference is 88cm. (Fig. A3)
  8. Find the angle subtended at the centre of a circle of radius 21cm by an arc of length 33cm. (Fig. A1)
  9. A wire is bent into a circle of radius 28cm, then rebent into a square. Find the side of the square.
  10. Find the diameter of a circle whose area equals the sum of the areas of two circles of radii 3cm and 4cm.

SA-II (3 marks) — 8 Qs

  1. A cow is tied with a 14m rope at the corner of a rectangular field. Find the area it can graze. (Fig. A6)
  2. Find the area of the segment of a circle of radius 21cm if the arc subtends 60° at the centre. (Fig. A5)
  3. The minute hand of a clock is 14cm long. Find the area swept by it in 20 minutes. (Fig. A7)
  4. A chord of a circle of radius 14cm subtends 60° at the centre. Find the area of the major segment. (Fig. A5)
  5. Find the area of a sector whose radius is 7cm and arc length is 11cm. (Fig. A1)
  6. A ring-shaped racetrack has inner and outer circumferences of 352m and 396m. Find the width of the track. (Fig. A8)
  7. In a circle of radius 21cm, an arc subtends 60° at the centre. Find (i) the arc length (ii) the sector area (iii) the corresponding segment area. (Fig. A5)
  8. A wheel of radius 42cm makes how many complete revolutions in moving 26.4 km?
